title: Aesthetics of the Senses
description: Focuses on the biological and environmental triggers of pleasure.

subtags.description: Specific smells like wet earth, jasmine, or musk that evoke emotional and sensory responses.
examples: Fragrance of wet earth after rain
Use of jasmine or sandalwood scents
Association of smell with memory and mood

subtags.description: Pleasure derived from sound, including ornaments, birds, musical tones, and ambient auditory elements.
The arrangement of a room or the visual appearance of a person, including color, symmetry, and aesthetic presentation.
examples: Visual harmony of clothing and ornaments
Overall presentation of a person or space

subtags.description: Sensations of touch, including softness, hardness, smoothness, and temperature of objects and surfaces.
Taste experiences, including wines, juices, betel, and other flavorful substances.
examples: Use of betel for taste and refreshment
Combination of sweet, sour, and aromatic tastes

subtags.description: Passages where senses overlap, such as describing sound as 'sweet' or colors as 'warm', blending sensory experiences.
examples: Describing music as sweet or soft

subtags.description: Use of moonlight, lamps, shadows, or darkness to influence mood and perception.
examples: Use of lamps for warmth and intimacy

subtags.description: Specific flowers used for their mood-altering fragrance and symbolic associations.
examples: Use of jasmine or lotus flowers

subtags.description: Descriptions of complexion, sweat, radiance, and surface qualities of the body as perceived visually and tactilely.
examples: Glow or radiance of the skin
Natural perspiration as a sensory element

subtags.description: Use of fans, water-sprays, cool floors, and other environmental adjustments to enhance comfort and sensory pleasure.
examples: Using fans or breezes for cooling
